issues.problem: Splatfacto split/duplicate ordering differs from the official code. Official split_gaussians shrinks the scales of the Gaussians it splits in place (self.scales[split_mask] = log(exp/1.6)) before dups is computed from self.scales. So (a) a split Gaussian whose max scale/1.6 <= densify_size_thresh (0.01 < smax <= 0.016 Nerfstudio units) is also duplicated, giving 3 children (2 split samples plus a surviving copy of the shrunk original; only the original index is culled); (b) a small Gaussian that is split because of its screen size gets a duplicate with the shrunk scale. The port computes dups = small & high before splitting and duplicates the unshrunk original, so case (a) never happens.
issues.evidence: official splatfactow_model.py:620-637 (dups computed after split_gaussians), 778-780 (in-place shrink), 662-673 (splits_mask culls only the original indices). On the 2k smoke checkpoint, 9.1% of Gaussians are in the band (0.01, 0.016]·(1/s) and 9.2% are above it, so roughly half of split candidates would get an extra duplicate in the official code. The splatfacto-refine probe splits at scale 0.05 (0.031 after the split), so it cannot see this.
issues.fix: Follow the code: smax_after = where(splits, smax/1.6, smax); dups = (smax_after <= thr/s) & high; give the duplicates the shrunk scales (or split first and duplicate the original indices with shrunk scales). Add a probe Gaussian at scale 0.014 with a high gradient and expect 3 children.

issues.problem: On crop views the official code renders the full W×H image, normalises radii by max(H, W) and sets last_size to (H, W). The port uses the crop size (H, W//2). For landscape images with H > W//2, this inflates max_2D by up to W/H (about 1.5×), which means more screen-size splits and culls (0.05 / 0.15). It also scales the densify-gradient factor 0.5·max(last_size) by H/W whenever the last render before a refinement is a crop. Gaussians that appear only in the right half are visible in the official code, with zero gradient, so they increment vis_counts there but not in the port.
issues.evidence: official after_train / get_outputs use the camera W,H; masked views are 10/773 (Brandenburg Gate) and 21/851 (Sacre Coeur) of training renders.
issues.fix: In accumulate, use (h, 2*w) for outputs['masked_view'] frames when normalising and in last_size. The vis_counts difference can be recorded as a gap.

issues.problem: The alpha loss was 0 throughout the smoke runs. Its formula matches the code exactly: the same [0,1] range, the robust-masked gt, the render-resolution frame, the raw unclamped SH background, mean_c < 0.003, box 3 'same' > 0.6, and alpha not detached. Zero is the expected early behaviour, not a bug, but nothing records whether it ever turns on.
issues.evidence: GPU check on evidence/smoke-1 (12 training views, full and 1/4 res): alpha < 0.1 at 0% of pixels; |gt-bg| < 0.003 at 0.003% of pixels; 0 pixels selected; the background lies in [0.21, 1.27] with 8% of it above 1, where the final clamp blocks the gradient. With the Gaussians covering every pixel, the background gets no gradient, so it cannot fit the sky to within 0.003. The official code has the same dynamics.
issues.fix: Log the number of selected pixels (and the alpha-loss value) in the benchmark; if it stays 0 through 55k, state that the C3 alpha loss was inactive rather than claim it.

issues.problem: 21.47 is a right-half score and gsplat's 19.79 is a full-image score, so these two numbers are not comparable. The comparable pair is the full-image 21.63 vs 19.79.
issues.fix: Quote 21.63 vs 19.79 (full image) when comparing with gsplat.

issues.problem: The port duplicates small-but-screen-large Gaussians before splitting them, so the duplicate keeps the original scale; in the code it gets the scale divided by 1.6. This is subsumed by the major fix above.

summary: A careful port that matches the code almost everywhere. Verified against the official code: the appearance and background MLP architectures and heads, the SH frames, the robust mask (thresholds, statistic, in-place-zero semantics, step boundaries), the alpha loss formula, the LR table and its step indexing, the resolution/SH/reset/densify windows, opacity init 0.1 and 3-NN scale init, and the Nerfstudio normalisation (s = 0.2286 reproduced independently from the same 773 poses the official code uses). The crop-view protocol reproduces the official masked loss, robust mask and alpha loss exactly. Evaluation (right half, jointly trained embedding, no TTO, torchmetrics-equivalent metrics) matches the official config (eval_right_half=True). The alpha loss being 0 at 2k is the expected dynamic (alpha >= 0.1 everywhere, so the background is not yet fitted to within 0.003), not a bug. One major deviation: the official splatfacto split shrinks scales in place before computing duplicates, so Gaussians in the (0.01, 0.016] band get an extra duplicate; the port omits this, and it affects about half of the split candidates. Minor: densification statistics on crop views use the crop size instead of the full image size.
